Use caution and monitor patients when administering P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrates alongside other drugs, as even minimal changes in drug concentration can result in severe or life-threatening toxicities. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates in such cases. 2. Turmeric can increase the levels or effects of quinine by interfering with hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Ustekinumab may alter the formation of CYP450 enzymes due to increased cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. When initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients receiving CYP450 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index, therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 4. Both vardenafil and quinine can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary to mitigate the risk of arrhythmias. 5. Viloxazine, a weak CYP3A4 inhibitor, can increase the systemic exposure of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, including quinine. Monitor and adjust the substrate dose as clinically indicated. 6. Voclosporin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for potential cardiac effects. 7. Vonoprazan, a weak CYP3A inhibitor, can increase the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised when using sensitive CYP3A substrates. 8.
